attribution.note: Zitron's own words, presented as fact in his post.

semantics.note: 'About $5 billion a year' matches the stated figure. It is a present-tense factual assertion.

contract.note: Reading 'burns' as net cash burn is an ordinary financial reading, but the speaker's linked sourcing points to loss estimates. That choice of metric decides the result. The contract flags this openly.

evidence.note: Dated Sept 2024 report of a projected 2024 loss of about $5B that excludes some expenses. It is a forecast of losses, not a realised full-year net cash burn figure.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is a mid-year projection of 2024 accounting losses, not a reconciled full-year cash-burn figure. Under the contract's cash-burn metric nothing confirms or refutes about $5B. Even on a loss reading, the item is a projection, not a realised result.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: A present-tense assertion about OpenAI's business viability with no horizon. The normalisation is faithful, though the claim is evaluative in nature.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 'lacked a commercially credible route' is a fair plain reading and avoids turning it into a 'never profitable' forecast. The speaker supplied no definition of path, so interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: Reports a management projection of profit by 2029. A company projection cannot establish or exclude a feasible route.

reviews.rationale: The packet holds only a secondhand report of management projections. There is no independently examined financial model showing whether a credible route to profit existed in early 2025, so the evidence does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. The Information's point that follows is separate and is not part of this claim.

semantics.note: Preserves the $2 Google business figure, the Microsoft consumer scope, the forcing claim and the demand claim.

contract.note: Treating 'forcing' as default bundling, with alternatives counting as a qualification, is fair. So is the general-demand reading. Whether forcing means default or unavoidable bundling affects the Microsoft part.

evidence.note: Google disclosure: Business Standard rises $2 per user per month with Gemini included by default. Covers one plan example, not all plans.
Microsoft disclosure: Copilot bundled into Personal and Family plans, with a price rise at renewal. It also mentions non-Copilot options.
Confirms the $3 rise but shows Classic plans without AI at old prices for existing subscribers. This qualifies an absolute reading of forcing.

reviews.rationale: Holds: Google's $2 Gemini-inclusive increase (Business Standard example) and Microsoft's Copilot-justified consumer price rise with default bundling. Qualified: existing Microsoft subscribers could keep Classic plans without AI. Unverified: no representative evidence that affected customers did not want the features.

semantics.note: '100% sure... will return' is a firm, scoreable forecast with no deadline. The intent clause is given as the reason, not as a condition.

contract.note: Counting restored profiles or a successor set of Meta-operated character profiles, but not a general assistant or a feed, is a fair reading of 'these chatbots'.

evidence.note: 2023 Meta post defining the original Meta-managed AI profiles. Sets the scope only.
Jan 2026 Meta update says a new version of AI characters is being built. No launch of public Meta-operated profiles is shown.
Vibes is an AI-video feed launched in 2025. It bears on the stated rationale but is a different product from the profiles.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given. The packet shows Meta building new AI characters but no dated launch of Meta-operated character profiles, and no event that rules out a return. Their absence so far is not failure, so the forecast stays unresolved.
